name: Absence plan
definition: The rules engine behind an absence type: who is eligible, how entitlement is earned or granted, and how it is paid.

name: Absence type
definition: What the worker actually selects when requesting leave — 'Annual Leave', 'Sick Leave', 'Maternity Leave'. Must be associated with at least one absence plan.

name: Abstract role
definition: A role held by virtue of being a person in the system rather than because of a specific job — Employee, Line Manager, Contingent Worker.

name: Accrual band
definition: A rule within an accrual plan granting different accrual rates to different populations, usually by length of service.

name: Accrual plan
definition: A plan where workers accumulate leave over time, with rules for accrual rate, ceilings, and carryover.

name: Area of Responsibility (AOR)
definition: An assignment of responsibility for a defined population, used to drive both access and routing.

name: Assignment
definition: The record carrying the actual job details: business unit, department, job, position, grade, location, manager, working hours, assignment status, and the standing data payroll reads.
watchOut: Putting person-level data on the assignment or assignment-level data on the person. Knowing which lives where is the whole skill.

name: Attrition / turnover
definition: The rate at which people leave the organization over a period, usually expressed annually as a percentage.

name: Balance
definition: An accumulated total of element results over a defined period and dimension — for example gross pay year-to-date, or taxable earnings month-to-date.
watchOut: Expecting balances to survive a global transfer. They do not.

name: BI Publisher (BIP)
definition: Oracle's formatted reporting tool, combining a SQL-based data model with a layout template to produce pixel-controlled output.
watchOut: Treating them as interchangeable. Using OTBI for a payslip or BIP for a quick headcount list are both wrong answers in an interview.

name: Bracket elimination for high earners
definition: A rule progressively removing access to the lower tax bands as net taxable income rises above defined thresholds.
watchOut: Building a naive progressive calculation that applies every band to every employee. It will be wrong for senior staff, which is exactly who notices.

name: Bursting
definition: Splitting one BI Publisher report run into many individual outputs, each delivered separately.

name: Business unit (BU)
definition: An operational grouping used for processing transactions, sharing reference data such as jobs and grades, and controlling data access. Not a legal registration.
watchOut: 'A business unit is just another word for department.' No. A BU is a processing and access construct; departments sit below it on the org chart.

name: Carryover
definition: The rules governing how much unused leave transfers into the next plan term, and when it expires.

name: Casual leave
definition: Short-notice leave for unforeseen circumstances.

name: Centers of Excellence (CoE)
definition: Specialist HR teams owning policy in a specific domain — Compensation & Benefits, Talent Acquisition, Learning & Development, Organization Development.

name: Change request
definition: A formal request to alter agreed scope, with its impact on time and cost assessed.

name: Compensatory plan
definition: A plan tracking earned compensatory time off, given instead of paying overtime.

name: Concurrent employment
definition: One person holding multiple simultaneous assignments under the same work relationship, or multiple work relationships across different legal employers.

name: Configuration workbook
definition: The structured document recording every configuration decision and its agreed values.

name: Costing
definition: The allocation of payroll results to accounting segments so the cost lands in the right place in the general ledger.

name: CRP (Conference Room Pilot)
definition: A structured demonstration of the configured system to the client using their own data and scenarios.

name: Cutover
definition: The sequenced set of activities moving the client from the legacy system to the new one.

name: Data role and security profile
definition: Where a job role says what a user can do, the data role and security profile say which records they can do it to.

name: Department
definition: An organization to which workers are assigned — the box on the org chart that a person actually sits in.

name: DFF (Descriptive Flexfield)
definition: A configurable extra field added to a standard object without customization.

name: Division
definition: A broader grouping above departments, usually aligned to a product line, business segment, or geography.

name: Duty role
definition: A granular building block granting specific privileges, aggregated into job and abstract roles.

name: Effective date
definition: The date on which a change becomes true in the real world — not the date it was typed into the system.
watchOut: 'Effective date is the date I entered it.' No — the system tracks the entry date separately.

name: Egyptian annual leave entitlement
definition: The statutory leave ladder under Labour Law No. 14 of 2025.

name: Element
definition: The definition of a single thing that can appear on a payslip: a salary, an allowance, a deduction, or an informational item.
watchOut: Creating an element and expecting it to appear for employees. Nothing happens until eligibility is defined and an entry exists.

name: Element classification
definition: The category assigned to an element — earnings, deduction, information — which controls processing order and how it feeds balances.

name: Element eligibility (element link)
definition: The rule defining which population of workers an element applies to, based on criteria such as payroll, legal employer, grade, job, or department.
watchOut: Defining eligibility too narrowly at build time and then needing to change it after entries already exist, which is considerably messier.

name: Element entry
definition: The actual assignment of an element to a specific person, with its values and dates.

name: Eligibility profile
definition: A reusable set of criteria determining whether a person qualifies for an absence plan — based on grade, job, department, location, length of service, and similar.

name: End of contract
definition: A fixed-term contract reaching its expiry date. Nobody terminates it; it simply lapses.
watchOut: Treating all three exit routes as one 'termination' transaction. They have different downstream calculations.

name: End of Service Benefit (EOSB) / gratuity
definition: A statutory lump sum payable to departing employees in Gulf countries, calculated on length of service and final wage.
watchOut: Importing EOSB logic into an Egyptian design, or assuming Egypt has gratuity. It does not work that way.

name: End-dating
definition: Closing a record as of a date rather than deleting it, so that history is preserved.
watchOut: 'I'll just delete the wrong record.' In a date-effective SaaS system you end-date, correct, or reverse. Deletion is rare, restricted, and usually the wrong instinct.

name: Enterprise
definition: The single top node of the entire organizational structure. There is exactly one enterprise per Oracle HCM implementation, and everything else is defined beneath it.
watchOut: Do not describe the enterprise as 'the company'. The company is the legal entity. The enterprise is the whole group.

name: Fast Formula
definition: Oracle's rule language used to express calculations and conditions — payroll rates, accrual rules, eligibility logic.
watchOut: 'Fast Formula is a programming language to master upfront.' It is a per-context rule language — approach it through examples.

name: Final settlement
definition: The calculation of everything owed to a leaver: final salary, unused leave payout, any severance or end-of-service benefit, minus outstanding deductions such as loans.

name: Fit-gap analysis
definition: Comparing client requirements against delivered functionality and documenting where the product fits, where it does not, and what will be done about the gaps.

name: Form 1 and Form 6
definition: The statutory notifications filed with social insurance on hiring (Form 1) and on termination (Form 6).

name: Freeze period
definition: A window during which no changes are permitted in the legacy system, so that final data migration is against a stable base.

name: FTE (full-time equivalent)
definition: A measure of workload rather than of people. An employee working 50% time is 0.5 FTE but still 1 headcount.
watchOut: Reporting FTE when the client asked for headcount, or the reverse. They are different numbers and both are 'correct'.

name: Global transfer
definition: Moving a worker from one legal employer to another — typically across countries. The source work relationship is terminated and a new one is created under the destination legal employer.
watchOut: Expecting balances to carry across. They do not — balances never span payroll relationships, so year-to-date figures start fresh in the new country.

name: GOSI
definition: The General Organization for Social Insurance — Saudi Arabia's social insurance authority.

name: Grade
definition: A level in the organization's hierarchy, used to control compensation ranges and eligibility for benefits or allowances.
watchOut: 'Grade equals salary.' Grade is a level. Money attaches to it through rate ranges and the salary basis — the two are linked but distinct objects.

name: Grade step
definition: An increment within a single grade, used where progression happens in defined steps rather than across a continuous range. Steps are grouped into grade ladders.

name: HCM Extract
definition: A framework for extracting HCM data on a schedule for delivery to external systems.

name: HDL (HCM Data Loader)
definition: Oracle's bulk data loading tool, using structured .dat files uploaded as a zip.
watchOut: 'Functional means no technical work.' In HCM the market pays a premium for functional consultants who handle HDL, formulas, and reporting themselves.

name: Headcount
definition: A raw count of people, regardless of how much each one works. One person equals one headcount.

name: HRBP (HR Business Partner)
definition: An HR professional embedded with a specific business division as its strategic HR contact.

name: HSDL (HCM Spreadsheet Data Loader)
definition: A spreadsheet-based interface over the same loading framework, aimed at business users.

name: Hypercare
definition: An intensive support period immediately after go-live with heightened staffing and response times.

name: Input value
definition: A field on an element that holds the data the calculation needs — typically amount, rate, percentage, or number of units.

name: Insurable wage
definition: The portion of pay on which social insurance contributions are calculated, bounded by a statutory floor and ceiling.
watchOut: 'Contributions apply to full gross salary.' They do not — they apply to the capped insurable wage. This is the most common calculation error in Egyptian payroll.

name: Iqama and visa-linked employment data
definition: Residency permit and visa information that must be tracked, with expiry alerting, for expatriate employees.

name: Job
definition: A generic definition of a role, independent of the organization chart. Carries attributes such as grade range, qualifications, and job family.
watchOut: Never define a job as a specific seat. That is a position.

name: Job family
definition: A grouping of related jobs sharing similar characteristics — for example all finance jobs, or all engineering jobs.

name: Job role
definition: A role reflecting a job someone does in the organization — HR Specialist, Line Manager, Payroll Manager.

name: Journey
definition: A configurable checklist of tasks assigned to a person around an event — onboarding, transfer, offboarding.

name: Leave encashment
definition: Paying out unused leave in cash instead of taking the time off.

name: Legal employer
definition: A legal entity that has been explicitly classified as an employer. This is the entity that legally hires workers and appears on employment contracts.
watchOut: Treating the two as synonyms. They are related but not interchangeable, and the difference is exactly what the question is testing.

name: Legal entity
definition: An organization recognized by law that can own assets, sign contracts, incur liabilities, and be sued. Created in Oracle through the Legal Entity Configurator.
watchOut: A legal entity on its own does not employ anybody. It has to be classified as a legal employer before a single person can be hired into it. This distinction is the most commonly missed point in the whole area.

name: Legislative Data Group (LDG)
definition: A partition that isolates payroll and related legislative data by country. All payroll configuration — elements, balances, formulas — lives inside exactly one LDG.
watchOut: Thinking you can reuse one element library globally. You cannot. Each LDG is its own world.

name: Location
definition: A physical work site, with an address, attached to positions and assignments.

name: Lookup type and lookup code
definition: Configurable lists of values used in dropdowns across the application.

name: Martyrs & Victims Fund contribution
definition: A small statutory employee deduction of 0.05% of gross pay.

name: Maternity leave
definition: Paid leave around childbirth.

name: Minimum wage and mandatory annual increment
definition: The statutory wage floor and the legally required yearly increase.
watchOut: Calculating the mandatory increment on full gross. It is on the social insurance wage.

name: Mudad
definition: The Saudi platform supporting wage protection and payroll compliance.

name: Nitaqat / Saudization
definition: The Saudi quota system requiring employers to maintain minimum percentages of Saudi national employees, with a colour-banded compliance rating.

name: No entitlement plan
definition: A plan that tracks absences without maintaining a balance or providing entitlement — typically for unpaid leave.

name: NOSI
definition: The National Organization for Social Insurance — the Egyptian authority administering social insurance under Law 148 of 2019.

name: Notice period
definition: The advance written warning either party must give before terminating an indefinite-term contract.
watchOut: Configuring notice rules from a secondary English-language source without verification. Statutory detail is the one area where being confidently wrong is expensive.

name: Oracle True Cloud Method
definition: Oracle's current implementation methodology for Fusion Cloud projects.
watchOut: 'Consultants design the best system.' Consultants get decisions made and documented; the client owns the design.

name: Org chart
definition: The visual representation of reporting hierarchy — who reports to whom.

name: OTBI
definition: Oracle Transactional Business Intelligence — ad-hoc reporting and analysis directly against live HCM data, using pre-built subject areas.
watchOut: Using OTBI for a payslip. Wrong tool — that is BI Publisher.

name: Parallel run
definition: Running the new system's payroll alongside the legacy payroll for the same period and reconciling the two, line by line.
watchOut: 'Go-live means done.' Hypercare and the first live payroll after parallel are the actual finish line.

name: Payment process / bank file
definition: The process that generates the actual payment instruction file sent to the bank.

name: Payroll definition
definition: The configuration of a payroll's calendar: its frequency, period start and end dates, cut-off dates, and payment date.

name: Payroll relationship
definition: A parallel object linking the person to a payroll statutory unit (PSU). It is the highest level of the payroll employment model and groups a person's assignments for statutory calculation and reporting.
watchOut: Thinking payroll runs against the assignment. It runs against the payroll relationship, aggregating across the assignments grouped within it.

name: Payroll run
definition: The process that calculates gross-to-net for a population of workers for a given period.

name: Payroll Statutory Unit (PSU)
definition: A legal entity classified as responsible for paying workers, including remitting payroll tax and social insurance to the authorities.
watchOut: Assuming one PSU per country automatically. A group with three registered companies in Egypt may well have three PSUs.

name: Person
definition: The record of a human being, held once globally. Carries what is true of the human regardless of any employer: name, date of birth, national ID, personal contact details, nationality.
watchOut: 'There is an employee table.' There is not. There is a person, a work relationship, and an assignment.

name: Personal exemption
definition: An annual amount deducted from income before applying the tax brackets.

name: Position
definition: A specific, individual seat: a job tied to a particular department and location, which exists whether or not anyone currently fills it.
watchOut: 'Job and position are synonyms.' They are not, and this is the fastest way to look unprepared in front of a trainer. Job = what the work is. Position = a specific seat doing it.

name: Prepayments
definition: The process that takes payroll run results and distributes them across the person's payment methods, ready for payment.

name: Probation
definition: An initial period during which either party may end the employment with lighter obligations than after confirmation.
watchOut: Assuming probation can be extended by agreement. Under the 2025 law it cannot.

name: Progressive tax brackets
definition: Egypt's seven-band salary tax scale applied to annual net taxable income.
watchOut: 'Tax is a flat monthly percentage.' It is annual, progressive, exemption-adjusted, and reconciled.

name: Qiwa
definition: The Saudi Ministry of Human Resources digital labour platform, handling contracts, work permits, and establishment services.

name: Qualification plan
definition: A plan where workers qualify for entitlement on an event, with payment percentages that can vary by band, rather than accruing a balance.

name: Quarterly update (26A–26D)
definition: Oracle's fixed quarterly release cycle for Fusion Cloud applications.

name: QuickPay
definition: A process that runs payroll for a single person outside the main run.

name: RAID log
definition: A tracking log of Risks, Assumptions, Issues, and Dependencies.

name: Reconciliation
definition: Comparing outputs between two systems or two runs and explaining every difference.

name: Redwood
definition: Oracle's current user experience and design system, progressively replacing older pages.

name: Resignation
definition: Employee-initiated termination of the employment relationship.

name: REST API
definition: Oracle's web service interface for programmatic read and write access to HCM data.
watchOut: 'I can query the database directly.' There is no SQL Developer connection to a SaaS pod. Your query paths are OTBI, BIP data models, extracts, and REST.

name: Retroactive change (retro)
definition: A change entered with an effective date in the past, after payroll has already been processed for that period.
watchOut: Assuming retro only adds money. It can also create a recovery when a change reduces pay.

name: Salary basis
definition: The configuration that determines how salary is stored, quoted, and paid — annual, monthly, or hourly — and which element it feeds.

name: Sandbox
definition: An isolated workspace for making and testing configuration changes before publishing them to the live environment.

name: Shared services / HR Operations
definition: A centralized team handling transactional HR work — payroll processing, data entry, tier-one queries — for the whole organization.
watchOut: Treating them as low-level administrators. They hold the operational knowledge no document captures.

name: Sick leave
definition: Paid leave for illness, with payment rates varying by duration.

name: SIT (System Integration Testing)
definition: Testing that the configured system works end to end, including integrations with other systems.

name: Social insurance contribution rates
definition: The statutory percentages contributed by employee and employer on the insurable wage.

name: Solid-line vs dotted-line reporting
definition: Solid line is the formal line manager who owns performance and compensation decisions. Dotted line is a secondary, functional reporting relationship without that authority.

name: Source system key vs person number
definition: The source system key identifies a record in the legacy system for load and reconciliation purposes; the person number is Oracle's own identifier.
watchOut: 'Data conversion is a side task.' It is routinely the thing that delays go-live.

name: Subject area
definition: A pre-built, governed data model in OTBI exposing a business domain such as workforce management or absence.

name: Tax Reporting Unit (TRU)
definition: The reporting face of a PSU toward tax and statutory authorities. TRUs are created under a PSU and are what statutory reports and deduction cards actually reference.

name: Termination
definition: Employer-initiated ending of employment, with or without cause.

name: Test script
definition: A step-by-step document defining what to do, what data to use, and what result to expect.

name: UAT (User Acceptance Testing)
definition: Client-executed testing against agreed scripts to confirm the system meets requirements.
watchOut: 'Testing is the QA team's job.' Not on a functional implementation.

name: Ulrich model
definition: The dominant model for structuring an HR function into three parts: HRBPs, Centers of Excellence, and Shared Services.

name: Universal health insurance
definition: A separate contributory health insurance scheme being progressively rolled out across governorates.

name: Update vs correction
definition: An update creates a new dated record and preserves history. A correction overwrites the existing record as if the previous value was never true.
watchOut: Using correction to fix a real-world change, thereby destroying legitimate history.

name: Value set
definition: A definition constraining what values a flexfield segment can accept.

name: Work relationship
definition: The link between a person and one legal employer, carrying a worker type and the start date of that employment. Terminating employment end-dates the work relationship.
watchOut: Confusing termination of a work relationship with deletion of the person. The person record survives; the work relationship is end-dated.

name: Work terms
definition: An optional intermediate layer between the work relationship and the assignment, used to group employment terms such as payroll and compensation across multiple assignments.
watchOut: Assuming every implementation has work terms. Many do not — the two-tier model omits this layer entirely.

name: Worker types
definition: The category recorded on a work relationship: employee, contingent worker, pending worker, or non-worker.

name: WPS and SIF file
definition: The Wage Protection System and the Salary Information File format used to prove salaries were paid correctly and on time.

name: Grain
definition: What a single row of a table represents, said in one sentence — one order, one order line, one product per store per day.
watchOut: A join can change the grain without warning. If you cannot state the grain after a join, do not sum anything.

name: Primary key
definition: The column or set of columns that uniquely identifies a row, and therefore proves what the grain is.
watchOut: A column called ID is not automatically unique. Count rows versus count distinct before you trust it.

name: Foreign key
definition: A column that points at another table's primary key, which is what makes a join possible.
watchOut: Many analytics databases do not enforce them, so an orphaned key that matches nothing is perfectly possible.

name: Surrogate key
definition: A meaningless generated number used as the key, as opposed to a natural key like an email address that carries business meaning.
watchOut: Natural keys change — people change email addresses — and a key that changes breaks every row referencing it. Join on surrogates, report on naturals.

name: Cardinality
definition: How many rows on one side of a relationship correspond to a row on the other: one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many.
watchOut: Getting it wrong is the usual cause of an inflated total.

name: Tidy data
definition: One variable per column, one observation per row, one value per cell.
watchOut: A column header that is itself a data value — Jan, Feb, Mar — is the most common violation.

name: Long and wide form
definition: Wide encodes a variable in the column headers; long stores it as values in a column, with one row per observation.
watchOut: Pivot tables, Power BI and most charting tools expect long. Unpivot before you analyse, not after.

name: NULL
definition: A marker for a value that was never recorded — distinct from zero, which is a measurement, and from an empty string.
watchOut: Filling NULLs with zero is a modelling decision you have to be able to defend, not a cleanup step.

name: Logical processing order
definition: The order the engine resolves a query in — FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT — which is not the order you write it in.
watchOut: It explains almost every beginner error, starting with why a SELECT alias cannot be used in WHERE.

name: WHERE versus HAVING
definition: WHERE discards rows before grouping; HAVING discards groups after it.
watchOut: A condition on an aggregate can only go in HAVING, because the aggregate does not exist until GROUP BY has run.

name: GROUP BY
definition: Collapses rows into one row per distinct combination of the grouping columns.
watchOut: Every selected column must be grouped by or aggregated — otherwise the engine has no way to pick which value to show.

name: Aggregate function
definition: SUM, COUNT, AVG, MIN or MAX — a function that turns many rows into one value.
watchOut: They skip NULLs, so an average divides by the number of non-null rows, not the row count.

name: DISTINCT
definition: Removes duplicate rows from the output, after SELECT has built them.
watchOut: Reaching for it to hide duplication caused by a join treats the symptom; the grain is what is wrong.

name: Alias scope
definition: Where a name defined in SELECT can be used — generally in ORDER BY, generally not in WHERE, GROUP BY or HAVING.
watchOut: This one genuinely varies by dialect, so check rather than assume.

name: Three-valued logic
definition: SQL conditions evaluate to true, false or unknown, and any comparison involving NULL is unknown.
watchOut: NOT IN against a list containing NULL is never true, so the query returns nothing at all and nothing errors. Use NOT EXISTS.

name: COUNT(*) versus COUNT(column)
definition: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) counts rows where that column is not NULL; COUNT(DISTINCT column) counts distinct non-null values.
watchOut: Three different questions. Interviewers ask because it tests whether you have thought about NULLs.

name: Inner join
definition: Keeps only rows that found a match on both sides.
watchOut: Silently drops rows that failed to match, which is how records disappear from a report unnoticed.

name: Left join
definition: Keeps every row from the left table, filling the right-hand columns with NULL where nothing matched.
watchOut: A condition on the right table in WHERE turns it back into an inner join. Put that condition in ON instead.

name: Full outer join
definition: Keeps unmatched rows from both sides, filling the gaps with NULL.
watchOut: Useful for reconciling two sources; check both directions for unmatched rows, not just one.

name: Cross join
definition: Pairs every row on the left with every row on the right, producing the product of the two row counts.
watchOut: Almost always an accident — usually a missing join condition — but deliberately useful for building a date scaffold.

name: Fan-out
definition: When a one-to-many join repeats each left row once per match, multiplying the rows.
watchOut: Correct join behaviour, and how totals silently double. Aggregate the many side to your grain before joining.

name: Anti-join
definition: The idiom for rows with no match: a left join followed by a WHERE that keeps only the NULL right-hand rows.
watchOut: This is the one case where filtering the right table in WHERE is deliberate rather than a bug.

name: Join key mismatch
definition: Keys that look equal but are not — trailing spaces, a text column joined to an integer, different case, stripped leading zeros.
watchOut: When a join returns too few rows, suspect the data before the SQL.

name: Window function
definition: A calculation across a set of rows that returns a value on every row instead of collapsing them, marked by the OVER clause.
watchOut: You cannot filter on one in WHERE or HAVING — both run before it is computed. Wrap it in a CTE.

name: PARTITION BY
definition: Splits the rows into independent groups so the window calculation restarts for each — the window equivalent of GROUP BY, except the rows survive.
watchOut: Omitting it makes the whole result set one partition, which is occasionally what you want and often not.

name: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK
definition: Three ways to number rows: never tie (1,2,3), tie and skip (1,2,2,4), tie and do not skip (1,2,2,3).
watchOut: ROW_NUMBER with no tiebreaker in the ORDER BY returns a different row between runs.

name: LAG and LEAD
definition: Return a value from an earlier or later row in the partition, which is how period-on-period change is written.
watchOut: They replace the self-join most people reach for first, in one line.

name: Frame clause
definition: How much of the partition the function sees for the current row — ROWS or RANGE BETWEEN some start AND some end.
watchOut: With an ORDER BY and no frame, the default is RANGE, which treats tied ordering values as one unit. On data with ties, a running total silently differs from ROWS.

name: Common table expression (CTE)
definition: A named query, written WITH name AS (...), that later parts of the statement can refer to.
watchOut: Not necessarily computed once — some engines inline it, so a CTE referenced three times may run three times.

name: Recursive CTE
definition: A CTE that refers to itself, used to walk a hierarchy such as an org chart or a category tree in a single query.
watchOut: Always give it a termination condition or a depth limit; an unbounded one will run until something stops it.

name: QUALIFY
definition: A clause in some warehouses that filters on a window function directly, without wrapping the query.
watchOut: Not standard SQL. Check your engine has it before writing it into anything shared.

name: XLOOKUP
definition: Excel's lookup function that takes a lookup array and a return array, defaults to exact match, and can look in either direction.
watchOut: Its predecessor VLOOKUP defaults to approximate match when the fourth argument is omitted, which returns confidently wrong answers on unsorted data.

name: INDEX and MATCH
definition: The older pairing that does what XLOOKUP does — MATCH finds the position, INDEX returns the value at it.
watchOut: Worth reading fluently even if you never write it, because inherited spreadsheets are full of it.

name: Excel Table
definition: A range formatted as a named object with typed columns, giving structured references like Sales[Revenue] that extend automatically.
watchOut: It removes the commonest serious spreadsheet bug: a formula whose hard-coded range stopped short of new rows.

name: Pivot table
definition: A drag-and-drop grouped aggregation, and the fastest way to explore an unfamiliar dataset.
watchOut: If it counts when you expected it to sum, there is a non-numeric value in the column.

name: Power Query
definition: The transformation engine shared by Excel and Power BI: import, clean, reshape and join, with every step recorded and repeatable.
watchOut: The highest-return thing an Excel user can learn, and it transfers directly to Power BI.

name: Volatile function
definition: A function such as NOW, TODAY, RAND, OFFSET or INDIRECT that recalculates on every change anywhere in the workbook.
watchOut: A common and invisible reason a workbook becomes slow.

name: Excel's limits
definition: 1,048,576 rows by 16,384 columns per sheet — though performance, and the absence of any audit trail, bite well before that.
watchOut: The moment a number matters to more than one person or must be reproduced next month, the answer stops being a spreadsheet.

name: Dynamic arrays and spilling
definition: One formula returning many results into neighbouring cells, which is what FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE and SEQUENCE rely on.
watchOut: A spill range needs empty cells to spill into, or it returns #SPILL!.

name: Fact table
definition: The table of events you measure — one row per sale, click or ticket — holding the numbers to aggregate and the keys pointing outward.
watchOut: Descriptive attributes belong in dimensions, not here.

name: Dimension table
definition: The table of things you slice by — products, customers, stores, dates — short, slow-changing and descriptive.
watchOut: Given a flat export, splitting the dimensions out of it is the first modelling job.

name: Star schema
definition: One fact table surrounded by dimension tables, each joined by a single key — the shape Power BI is built for.
watchOut: Both the engine's compression and its filter propagation assume it. A flat wide table is slower and harder to reason about.

name: Relationship cardinality
definition: Whether a relationship is one-to-many, one-to-one or many-to-many, and which side is which.
watchOut: A many-to-many usually means a bridge table is missing.

name: Cross-filter direction
definition: Which way a filter travels along a relationship — single, from the one side to the many, or both.
watchOut: Bidirectional is the tempting fix for a slicer that does nothing and usually the wrong one: it creates ambiguous paths and slows queries.

name: Date table
definition: A dedicated dimension with one row per date and no gaps, marked as the model's date table.
watchOut: Without it, time-intelligence functions fail quietly at period boundaries rather than loudly.

name: Import versus DirectQuery
definition: Import loads a compressed copy into the model; DirectQuery leaves the data in the source and queries it per visual.
watchOut: Import is the default answer. DirectQuery costs latency, restricts DAX, and puts load on the source system.

name: Roche's Maxim
definition: Data should be transformed as far upstream as possible, and as far downstream as necessary.
watchOut: A calculation that gives the same answer whatever the user selects is a transformation, and belongs in Power Query rather than DAX.

name: Measure versus calculated column
definition: A calculated column is computed row by row at refresh and stored; a measure is computed at query time in the filter context of each cell.
watchOut: Writing a calculated column where a measure belongs bloats the model and produces a report that does not react to slicers.

name: Filter context
definition: The set of filters in force when a measure is evaluated — the cell's row and column, the slicers, the page and report filters.
watchOut: A total row is a different filter context, not the sum of the rows above it. That is why totals appear wrong when they are not.

name: Row context
definition: Having a current row to read columns from, which calculated columns and iterators have and measures do not.
watchOut: Row context does not filter anything by itself, which is why a bare column reference in a measure is an error.

name: CALCULATE
definition: The function that evaluates an expression in a filter context it has modified — the centre of the language.
watchOut: Its filter arguments replace existing filters on the same column rather than adding to them. Wrap in KEEPFILTERS to intersect instead.

name: Context transition
definition: CALCULATE converting an existing row context into the equivalent filter context.
watchOut: This is the mechanism behind most DAX behaviour that looks like magic, including why a measure called inside an iterator sees only one row.

name: Iterator functions
definition: The X functions — SUMX, AVERAGEX, MAXX, RANKX — which evaluate an expression once per row of a table and then aggregate.
watchOut: SUM adds a column that already exists; SUMX computes something per row first. Multiplying two columns needs the latter.

name: Time intelligence
definition: DAX functions such as SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, DATEADD and TOTALYTD that shift or accumulate over a date dimension.
watchOut: They require a marked, gapless date table, and without one they fail silently at period boundaries.

name: DIVIDE
definition: DAX's division function, which returns blank rather than an error when the denominator is zero.
watchOut: Use it instead of the / operator, or ship a visual full of errors the first time a category has no rows.

name: The business question
definition: The vague request turned into one sentence with a period, a comparison, a population and a decision attached.
watchOut: Agree that sentence before building. It is the specification, and usually the title of the chart.

name: Chart choice
definition: Bars for comparison across categories, lines for change over time, scatter for the relationship between two measures, a table when exact values matter.
watchOut: A pie is readable at two or three slices. Beyond that it is a bar chart pretending.

name: Truncated axis
definition: Starting a value axis somewhere other than zero, which exaggerates differences.
watchOut: Never on bars, which encode value by length. Acceptable on lines, which encode change by slope — if the axis is labelled honestly.

name: Dual axis
definition: Two different scales on one chart, one on each side.
watchOut: The apparent correlation is a function of where you set the two ranges. Two stacked charts on a shared time axis say it without the implication.

name: Data-ink
definition: Tufte's principle that most of the ink on a chart should represent data, and the rest should be as quiet as possible.
watchOut: Gridlines, borders, shadows and legends that merely repeat the labels are the usual offenders.

name: Dashboard versus report
definition: A dashboard is monitored regularly and should fit one screen; a report is read once and answers a question at whatever length that takes.
watchOut: Requests for a dashboard are frequently requests for a report. Ask how often they will look at it, and what they will do differently.

name: Sanity check
definition: Reconciling your total against a figure the business already trusts before you present it.
watchOut: If it does not match, find out why before the meeting — because someone in the room will.

name: Action and action reason
definition: Every change to an assignment is stamped with an action — Hire, Promotion, Transfer, Termination — and a client-defined reason underneath it. The action drives the flow; the reason makes later analysis possible.
watchOut: Reasons feel like optional paperwork during implementation and turn out to be the only way to answer 'why did attrition rise'. Configure them or lose the question for ever.

name: Assignment status
definition: The status on an assignment controlling whether it is active, suspended or inactive, and separately whether it is eligible for payroll processing.
watchOut: 'Active in HR but not paid' is a real and valid combination. It is also the usual explanation when somebody who should have been paid was not.

name: Employment model
definition: The enterprise-level setting that decides whether a worker can hold one assignment or several at once, and whether contracts are tracked separately. Two-tier single assignment covers most implementations.
watchOut: It can be overridden per legal employer, but changing it after workers exist is painful. Ask in the first workshop, not the third.

name: Enterprise Structures Configurator (ESC)
definition: An interview-style wizard that creates legal entities, classifies them as legal employers and payroll statutory units, and creates a legislative data group per country in one pass, with a technical summary to review before loading.
watchOut: Useful for a greenfield build, dangerous as a substitute for understanding — it makes defensible default choices the consultant then has to defend or unpick.

name: Last standard process date
definition: The date on a terminated payroll relationship after which ordinary payroll runs no longer pick the person up. A separate final close date stops everything, including corrections.
watchOut: Set the final close date too early and a legitimate late payment — a final bonus, a corrected settlement — cannot be made without reopening the record.

name: Legal jurisdiction
definition: A geographic area combined with the law that applies in it — Egypt income tax, Saudi social insurance. Every legal entity is registered against an identifying jurisdiction, and that registration number is what appears on statutory output.
watchOut: Jurisdictions and legal authorities must exist before the legal entity does. Discovering that mid-configuration costs an afternoon.

name: Organization tree
definition: A versioned parent-child arrangement of departments, organizations or positions. It draws the org chart and, more importantly, gives security profiles something to scope against.
watchOut: Trees must be published before they take effect, which is the usual explanation for 'I made the change and nothing happened'.

name: Primary assignment
definition: The flag marking which of a person's concurrent assignments is the main one. Reports, the org chart and most downstream integrations read it.
watchOut: Set on the minor of two jobs, it quietly reports the person under the wrong department indefinitely, and nothing in the application complains.

name: Reference data set
definition: A grouping of set-enabled configuration data — jobs, grades, locations, departments — assigned to one or more business units, which controls what can be selected on a transaction in that unit.
watchOut: Positions are the exception: they attach to a business unit directly, not through a set. Expecting positions to follow the job rules is a standard surprise.

name: Seniority date
definition: A configurable date that records continuous service, separate from the hire date, so that service can bridge a break in employment or carry across legal employers within a group.
watchOut: End-of-service gratuity and leave bands are calculated on service. Solving a rehire by back-dating the work relationship instead of setting a seniority date corrupts every headcount and accrual figure for that period.
